reasons: Directionally correct and correctly scoped: Section 14.2.1 imposes a fixed 300% multiple of SFJ's Development Costs on PB (our party) upon SFJ's termination for PB's material breach, and Section 14.4.2 expressly makes that sum SFJ's substitute for damages — squarely within the rule's detection guidance for a Customer-payable liquidated amount / minimum fee on termination, not a Vendor-payable service credit.

Not over-flagging: a 3x multiple of the funder's outlay, accelerated on breach and payable irrespective of Regulatory Approval, does not meet the fallback (a single, modest early-termination amount) and plausibly approaches the walk-away test of exceeding remaining contract value, so 'deviation' at high severity is the right classification.

Redline is valid, minimal and self-consistent: the only change is 300% -> 100% of Development Costs (changed-character ratio 0.068), leaving the Trial Data Package purchase mechanic, timing and the Approval Payment/Buy-Out economics intact; the text reads cleanly as amended.

Comment is accurate, in-tone and actionable: it explains the change, cites the Section 14.4.2 sole-remedy point that converts the multiple into a penalty, and anchors the substitute measure in the parties' own Section 14.2.9 formulation.

Minor, non-disqualifying notes: the playbook's literal fallback ('3 months' fees') has no analogue in a development-funding structure, so the drafter's substitute cap (return of costs actually paid or incurred) is a reasonable adaptation rather than the stated fallback — worth flagging to the negotiator; and the Section 14.2.9 cross-reference and the related 150%/25% mechanics in 14.2.6, 14.2.8.1 and 14.2.10 should be confirmed and aligned on the same basis as the rationale contemplates.
No double-counting: the parallel 300% at-will amount in Section 14.2.2 is expressly left to the termination-for-convenience rule.
